A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same perception-coherence representation-transfer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy-data transfer experiments, CIFAR10/CUB200 retrieval scores, and CIFAR100 classification results for the proposed method, alongside externally sourced baseline results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative studies of coherence estimation, student capacity, and temperature sensitivity.

M1.justification: The dissimilarity-based soft-ranking procedure, squared rank-discrepancy loss, and classification loss combination are retained (v1 Equation 3.4 and Appendix E.3; v2 Equation 4 and Appendix E.3). The smaller student variants evaluate the same method.

E1.justification: Coverage remains 2D/3D toy transfer, CIFAR10 retrieval, retrieval on CUB200’s first 30 classes, and CIFAR100 classification. New ablations reuse this coverage. Five-cluster toy data remain described despite their illustration’s removal. Table 6 evaluates CIFAR10/CUB200; its discussion’s CIFAR100 reference is inconsistent with the table.

E2.justification: Corresponding retrieval comparisons retain KD, FitNet, MKT, PKT, the multi-layer variants, and HKD. CIFAR100 retains KD, FitNet, VID, RKD, PKT, and CRD. Comparator membership matches between v1 Tables 4.1–4.3 and v2 Tables 1–3.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial controlled evaluation protocols: coherence estimation with batches of 4–256 against full-test-set values, one-/two-/three-layer students with global average pooling against the full student, and student temperatures from 0.001 to 10 with teacher temperature fixed. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 and Appendix E.4 add quantitative estimation-versus-batch-size analysis, student-capacity ablations, and temperature sensitivity tests. V1’s qualitative batch-size study is retained and moved into the main text. Its separate five-cluster transfer illustration, Figure E.1, is omitted.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 6 newly displays five coherence-estimation runs individually and their average; Table 4 supplies accompanying ± values without explicitly defining their statistical meaning. The five independent CIFAR100 training runs and existing uncertainty values are retained, with no reported increase.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values are unchanged in v2 Tables 1–3. Tables 4–6 add extensive coherence-estimation, capacity, and temperature results. For example, CUB200 mAP is 30.38 at newly tested temperature 0.5, while the original 28.42 at temperature 0.3 is retained. V1 Figure E.1’s qualitative result sequence is removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds a measurability assumption, an empirical difference-coefficient estimator, an unbiasedness proposition, and Theorem 4.1’s O(B^-1/2) expected-error claim with a new Appendix A proof argument and V-statistic lemma. Remark 3.2 also corrects the finite-distribution rank/CDF setup. Earlier order-preservation and stability results are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a specific mini-batch approximation-rate guarantee to the stated contributions. The conclusion drops v1’s claim to be the first attempt at topological deep learning for representation transfer and KD. The central method and competitive-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new results as linking coherence to student capacity and downstream performance, identifies excessive compression as a practical limitation, and explains extreme-temperature failures through vanishing gradients or near-linear soft rankings. It also adds a semantic rationale for ranking preservation and interprets the batch-size results as validating convergence.

D1.justification: Section 5.5 specifies network truncation and global average pooling for reduced students; Appendix E.4 specifies the temperature sweep and fixed-teacher control. Existing hardware, training times, principal hyperparameters, and the anonymous code-link destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Introduction to Information Retrieval (2008) for retrieval metrics and removes Zia et al.’s topological deep-learning review. It narrows the topology-related novelty positioning, while largely retaining the KD related-work discussion.

P1.justification: V2 selectively expands the abstract, introduction, and conclusion; separates theory into Section 4; moves the proposition proof and qualitative batch-size study into the main text; and removes the broader-impact statement. Much existing method, related-work, benchmark, and proof prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 adds explanatory Figures 1 and 3, estimation Figure 6, and Tables 4–6. V1 Figures E.3–E.4 move to main-text Figures 7–8, while Figure E.1 disappears. Typography, author formatting, table widths, and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new capacity and temperature ablations provide useful practical guidance missing from v1, and the explanatory diagrams improve accessibility. These gains are tempered by defects in the added convergence proof: Lemma A.1 treats two sums over the same batch as independent, leaving the new theoretical strengthening inadequately justified.
